summary: Evening 5xx surge caused by ephemeral-init throttling and KV-IO latency during mixed embed+stream workload
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 20:10 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses on several customer-facing streaming and embeddings routes for tenant NimbleChat (dedicated). Impact: customer reported degraded UX (stream disconnects and failed embedding uploads), increased error rate ~8% for API surface, and multiple customer calls. Initial triage shows apigw returning 502/503, upstream serving runtimes reporting worker exits and GPU eviction events.

Impact: Multiple sessions for NimbleChat experienced aborts, some calls retried by client and hit rate-limiting; billing-impacting errors and potential SLA breach if persistent.

Environment: prod us-east, dedicated pool for NimbleChat, autoscaler configured with reserved capacity + ephemeral burst pool. Mixed workload: many small embedding uploads (N=100k small batches) concurrently with low-latency streaming chat sessions.

Observed at: 2026-03-13 20:10 UTC — 21:05 UTC (first detection) and ongoing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a sustained mix of small-embedding uploads (~50-200 items per second) and concurrent streaming chat starts from a single tenant to prod us-east;
2) Configure client SDK to keep connections long-lived (keepalive enabled) and hedged retries with low backoff;
3) Observe accept-queue growth at api-gateway and increased latency to serving runtime prewarm endpoints;
4) Monitor kvcache disk/iostats on the serving nodes for bursts of reads/writes and NVMe iowait;
5) Watch runtime logs for worker init throttling, OOM eviction traces, and nvml GPU eviction events.
logs: apigw: 2026-03-13T20:12:02Z ERROR handler.go:412 upstream returned 502: upstream read timeout (accept queue=452 backlog=310)
runtime: 2026-03-13T20:12:05Z WARN runtime/worker.go:128 initThrottle: delaying new worker start for tenant NimbleChat due to burst=high prewarm_capacity=2
runtime: 2026-03-13T20:12:07Z ERROR runtime/gpu_manager.go:54 eviction: nvml: memory pressured -> evicting model redwood-v2-medium (pid=2719)
kvcache: 2026-03-13T20:12:10Z WARN kvcache/io.go:87 nvme_iowait=245ms writes_inflight=64 read_latency_p50=18ms read_latency_p99=420ms
apigw: 2026-03-13T20:13:01Z ERROR proxy.go:201 connection reset while streaming -> returning 503 to client
investigation_notes: 20:15 UTC - Initial hypothesis: combined high-rate embedding writes plus long-lived streams caused accept-queue growth on apigw and triggered runtime worker init throttling (initThrottle) to avoid overcommitting GPU memory; this introduced head-of-line blocking and retries from clients amplified error rate.

20:25 UTC - Observed NVMe iowait spikes correlating with kvcache write bursts — kvcache background compaction likely contending with prefetch writes, increasing worker init latency and causing proxies to time out.

20:35 UTC - SRE reproduced local load pattern in staging: when small-embed batch size <8 and many concurrent small batches, kvcache writes spike and accept-queue at apigw increases by 3-4x. Adding client-side jitter reduces peak but runtime still evicts hot models under high churn.

20:50 UTC - Noted hedged retry behavior from some SDK versions caused duplicate fanout to runtime at connection time; recommended immediate client guidance to disable aggressive hedging during ongoing mitigation.

Hypothesis: two interacting failure modes — kvcache IO saturation delaying prewarm/worker initialization + initThrottle protection that serializes worker starts — together cause apigw accept-queue collapse and 502/503 propagation.
comments: Customer (NimbleChat): 2026-03-13T20:18 UTC - 'Users are seeing a lot of disconnects. This is impacting conversations in our app. Can you investigate priority please?'
Support (Priya): 2026-03-13T20:22 UTC - Acknowledged, escalating to SRE. Please avoid redeploying any SDK changes for the next 30m and share any relevant request IDs if you see failures.

SRE (Marta Ruiz): 2026-03-13T20:30 UTC - Reproduced load in staging. Confirmed NVMe iowait and initThrottle delays. Spinning up additional prewarm capacity and temporarily increasing ephemeral burst pool for NimbleChat to reduce immediate errors.

SRE (Liam O'Connor): 2026-03-13T20:40 UTC - Applied temporary rate-limiter at apigw for tenant NimbleChat to smooth admit rate (token-bucket lowered from 1000r/s -> 400r/s) and disabled prefetch for tenant. Observed 5xx rate drop from ~8% -> ~1.6% in 4 minutes.
Support (Priya): 2026-03-13T20:50 UTC - Notified customer of temporary mitigations and asked them to confirm client-side retry/backoff settings. Opened ticket to track permanent fixes.
Customer (NimbleChat): 2026-03-13T21:00 UTC - 'Thanks — error rate dropped and our UX recovered. We'll apply backoff changes on our side and monitor.'
root_cause_summary: Interaction between kvcache NVMe IO saturation from high-rate small-embedding writes and serving-runtime worker init throttling (initThrottle) which serialized worker starts. Apigw accept-queue grew, causing upstream timeouts and 502/503 responses. Client hedged retries amplified the load during the window.
mitigation_actions: Applied tenant-scoped admission smoothing at apigw (token-bucket reduction) to reduce peak arrivals;
Increased ephemeral burst capacity for NimbleChat in the dedicated pool to reduce init contention;
Disabled kvcache prefetch for the tenant to lower background compaction pressure;
Advised customer to reduce hedged retry aggressiveness and add jitter on retries;
Monitored error rate and NVMe metrics for 1 hour post-mitigation.
resolution:
Temporary mitigations placed at 2026-03-13 20:40 UTC restored service to acceptable error rates for NimbleChat. Customer confirmed degraded UX resolved. Long-term fixes identified and assigned: runtime team to adjust initThrottle backoff and add leaky-bucket admit smoothing in runtime prewarm path (owner: @MartaRuiz, PR planned), kvcache team to tune compaction schedule under mixed embed+stream traffic, and platform team to add tenant-level burst shaping in apigw config.

Follow-up: Postmortem scheduled (Owner: Liam O'Connor) and timeline for permanent fixes: patch proposal by 2026-03-17, staging validation 2026-03-19, prod rollout week of 2026-03-23.
next_steps: 1) Runtime: implement less-aggressive initThrottle backoff and add parallel prewarm worker windows (tracker: GH PR #2439);
2) KVCACHE: add IO-smoothing heuristics when compaction overlaps with high write bursts;
3) APIGW: implement tenant burst shaping policy so dedicated tenants can be given smoother admission control;
4) Customer: deploy client SDK with reduced hedged retry and added jitter (support provided);
5) Ops: schedule postmortem and circulate findings to product and support teams.
owner_notes: Keep ticket open until runtime/kvcache patches are merged and validated in staging. Coordinate communication with NimbleChat through CS. Priority: ensure no regressions for other dedicated tenants during burst-smoothing rollout.
